headline: Everything B06 promises works when walked: 62 of 64 criteria pass, 1 fails (a storage warning with no words) and 1 couldn’t be reached; every suite is green and all 13 flows pass against the real Worker, API and database. But two guards on critical paths hold nothing: no suite notices if a failed backup starts counting as a backup (in /health/jobs, the watchdog and Settings), or if the Worker starts ticking the API every minute (D141). Five of nine new breakage checks survived. The eyes pass also found a toast hiding Export their data first in the Remove dialog, which isn’t B06’s code.

suites.security: pnpm security: audit, gitleaks (407 commits, no leaks), security lint all PASS; pnpm hygiene clean
suites.db: pgTAP 218/218; API 128 pass, 7 skipped (the body checks a GET or the tick doesn't take); route sweep green
suites.mutants: 56 of 58 killed (sweep); run 3's probes 4 of 9 killed

findings.title: No suite notices a failed backup being counted as a backup: not in /health/jobs, not in the watchdog, not in Settings → Data.
findings.detail: Two breakage checks survive. In `jobs_health()` (0009), dropping `AND r.status = 'ok'` from the backup's subquery makes the monitor's check pass on a failed backup. In `backupFacts()` (`apps/api/src/jobs/frames.ts`), dropping `eq(r.status, 'ok')` from the *last backup* query makes Settings → Data show a failed backup as the last one, and silences the backup watchdog, which reads the same `last`. Today the code is right: FLOW-R3-6 step 4 (the last good backup 49 h old, a failed one today) answers 503 *late backup*, and FLOW-R3-4 doesn't show today's failed run. But a failing `sen_ops` workflow that reports `failed` every night is exactly what §18's three guards exist for, and nothing would tell anyone if one of them regressed. pgTAP's *health sees the backup* and the API's health test only cover good or missing backups.
findings.evidence:
| `r3-health-counts-failed-backup` | db | **SURVIVED** | a failed backup keeps /health/jobs green |
| `r3-last-backup-counts-failed` | db | **SURVIVED** | Settings → Data shows a failed backup as the last backup |
Both logs: `Files=4, Tests=218 ... Result: PASS` then `Tests  128 passed | 7 skipped (135)`

findings.title: The Worker's only-when-due gate (D141) has no test: it can tick the API every minute and every suite stays green.
findings.detail: `Scheduler.cron()` (`apps/worker/src/scheduler.ts`) calls `/jobs/tick` only when `due(s, now)`. Replacing `if (!due(s, now) || this.ticking) return;` with `if (this.ticking) return;` survives: `clock.test.ts` tests the pure `due()`, but nothing drives the Durable Object's `cron()`, so nothing checks it uses it. Each tick wakes Neon for 5 minutes; a tick a minute keeps it awake around the clock, and at Neon's 0.25 CU minimum that is about 180 CU-hours a month against the free 100: the database would stop for the rest of the month. D141 was decided for exactly this. The same untested method also writes back the state it read before the tick (see finding 11).
findings.evidence:
| `r3-scheduler-ticks-every-minute` | unit | **SURVIVED** | the Worker ticks the API every minute, so Neon never sleeps (D141) |
log: `Tests  95 passed (95)`

findings.title: On the Members journey, the Undone toast covers “Export their data first” in the Remove dialog, while Remove stays visible (not B06’s code).
findings.detail: The eyes pass (G9, G10) and I both see it in the film of `members…/9`: from about frame 15 the *Undone* toast from the step before sits across the *Remove Hui Min?* sheet exactly over *Export their data first*, and stays for the toast’s life. The dialog asks whether to keep a copy before an irreversible delete, and the copy’s button is the one hidden. B06’s diff changes no toast, sheet or members code (members.tsx gains one lint comment), so this almost certainly stands on main; the diff run films only the branch, so main’s film wasn’t seen. Toasts over sheets recur elsewhere (G8, G13, G18, G22): the shared toast layer sits above sheets.
findings.evidence: qa/B06/eyes.md G9: “From frame 15 to the end, the Undone toast sits across the sheet exactly where Export their data first is. Only the top edge of that button shows above the toast, and Remove’s top half is covered too.” Verdict wrong; G10 the same.

findings.title: A relay pass whose signature is right only in its first byte is accepted, and no test notices.
findings.detail: In `verifyPass()` (`packages/core/src/realtime.ts`), comparing one byte of the HMAC instead of all 32 survives: the forged-pass tests change the whole signature, so they still fail on the first byte. With a one-byte check, about 256 tries forge a 5-minute pass to any `user:<id>` channel. The relay carries only topic names (no data), hence Minor, but it is the relay's only check. A test that flips the signature's last byte would hold it.
findings.evidence:
| `r3-pass-checks-one-byte` | unit | **SURVIVED** | a relay pass is accepted when only the first byte of its signature is right |
log: `Tests  95 passed (95)`

findings.title: The `jobs` topic's reload has no test: mapping it to nothing leaves Settings → Data stale after a job, with every suite green.
findings.detail: `TOPIC_QUERIES.jobs` (`apps/web/src/data/realtime.ts`) maps the scheduler's hint to the `settings` query. Changing it to `[]` survives the web suite. findings.title: The breakage check `push-token-shared` is decorative: it edits 0008, but 0010 replaced that function.
findings.detail: Run 2's fix redefined `push_token_claim()` in 0010 (`CREATE OR REPLACE`), so removing the DELETE from 0008's copy changes nothing in the database and the check survives every run. The live definition is guarded: the same edit in 0010 (`r3-push-token-shared-0010`) is killed by pgTAP (*the token is Ben's alone now*, *still one row*). Retarget the entry at 0010. The same trap waits for any check on a function a later migration replaces (`jobs_health`, `jobs_next_once`).

findings.title: In a preview, Settings → Data dates a backup from today by the made-up scenario's clock: “Sun, 25 Oct, 19:01” on 25 Oct, never “Today”.
findings.detail: With the api backend in a preview build, the fake still wraps the server and moves the app's clock to 18 Oct 2026 (`lib/clock.ts`, `data/fake/connect.ts`), so `momentLabel()` can't say *Today* or *Yesterday* for a real backup. The date and time shown are right, in KL, and the same from New York (FLOW-R3-4b). The owner verifies on the review alias, so he sees this. Production has no fake; I didn't run a production build against the API to confirm its label.

findings.title: Storage between 999,500,000 and 999,999,999 bytes reads “1000 MB”, not “1.00 GB”.
findings.detail: `formatBytes()` rounds MB below 10⁹ bytes, so the last half-megabyte under a gigabyte rounds up to 1000 MB.

findings.title: `/health/jobs` is open to anyone and costs one database query per call, so a stranger polling it keeps Neon awake.
findings.detail: Measured in the API metrics: every call, 200 or 503, makes one query. It has no rate limit or secret. This isn't new exposure: signed-out `GET /api/*` already makes one query on main's routes. The monitor checks it every 3 hours (docs/local.md). A shared secret in cron-job.org's request header would close it if Neon's hours ever run short.

findings.title: `Scheduler.cron()` saves the state it read before a tick once the tick returns, over whatever changed meanwhile.
findings.detail: Read, not reproduced. `await this.save(await this.tick(s, now))` writes `s` (read before the up-to-5-minute fetch) with the tick's answer. A `wake()` from the API during the tick is lost (run 1 named this half, note 12), and `lastCron` steps back to the tick's start over the crons saved while it ran. For a tick near 5 minutes the Worker's `/health` could briefly read *cron late*. It sits in the same untested method as finding 2.
findings.evidence: const s = { ...(await this.state()), lastCron: now }; ... await this.save(await this.tick(s, now));

findings.title: The one metrics flag (Members → Invite settles in 272 ms against 142) isn't B06's: the same mutations land at the same times on both builds.
findings.detail: Accepted, with measurement. Main's own samples settle before they first change (settle 142 and 130 ms, first change 248 and 224 ms): settle is the last DOM mutation, first change the paint, so on main the measured window closed before the sheet's later mutations. B06 changes the members screen only by a lint comment. Measured: tapping Invite with the CPU slowed 4×, three times on each side, gives 99 mutations of the same kinds on both, the first after 200 ms at 664 and 653 ms on the branch (warm runs) against 648 and 649 ms on main. Both are far under the 1000 ms limit. The diff run's other red tests fail on main too: `subscription` under the metrics config (`getByText('Claude Pro')` matches three elements) and `scan-more` catalogue timeouts. settings/claims' pixel change (firefly, mercury, copper) is the tab bar's label anti-aliasing, tree unchanged. The run also rewrote 86 trees, line endings only (`git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` is empty).

findings.detail: Settings → Data: each *Checks* row wants a line saying what it does; the *Updated* pill is faint in Instrument, Mercury and Copper dark, and its raised shadow reads as tappable; after *Schedule a test job* the screen never shows that the job ran (only the push says so); a member could be told their data is backed up.
